# Valley of Grace BioHub

The Valley of Grace is the founding BioHub of the Overberg BioRegion, anchored at Genadendal in Ward 2, Theewaterskloof Municipality, Western Cape, South Africa. It coordinates landscape-scale catchment restoration, biodiversity stewardship, and regenerative economic coordination in the below-dam Riviersonderend corridor between the Theewaterskloof Dam wall and the Breede River confluence.

## Priority Services

- water-yield: Below-dam catchment restoration through alien clearing, soil sponge restoration, water-efficient agriculture, and distributed water storage in the Riviersonderend corridor. Readiness: contractable-after-build-out.
- biodiversity-data: Cape Mountain Leopard corridor monitoring, iNaturalist surveys, and Guardians of Earth Nature Realm data across ~10,000 ha. Readiness: contractable-after-build-out.
- heritage-and-tourism: Leopard Corridor Destination Management Plan, Genadendal Learning Hub, and regenerative tourism anchored at heritage sites. Readiness: contractable-after-build-out.

## Current Seeks

- Verification methodology alignment with Conservation Alpha for below-dam SWSA tranche
- Landowner stewardship agreements across the Riviersonderend corridor
- Peer BioHub coordination on shared Water Retention Landscape methodology
- Mycelial Patronage counterparties

## Financial Instruments

- Cape Water Performance-Based Bond (FR31PB), JSE-listed April 2026, ZAR 2.5 billion — Africa's first nature-linked performance-based bond
- ZA-FiCom: three-phase financial commons (Phase 1 design)

## BioRegion

This BioHub operates within the Overberg BioRegion. For regional-level coordination, ecological profiles, and shared governance, see [at12-overberg.bioconomy.earth](https://at12-overberg.bioconomy.earth).
